newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INTERVIEW-Water shortage seen in Malaysia state.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Water shortage seen in Malaysia state.

text.p: The key Malaysian state of Selangor may face a critical water shortage next year due to high growth in demand, low pressure and pipe leakages, a company supplying water to the state said on Thursday.
"I would like to say here that based on our assessment, the water shortage problem will be critical next year," said Puncak Niaga Holdings Bhd's executive chairman Rozali Ismail.
Puncak Niaga is set to list on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange next month.

"The growth in water demand which has exceeded the state's projection, coupled with the problem of low pressure and pipe leakages, will give rise to a situation in 1998 where there will not be enough water to be supplied to consumers in the state," he told Reuters in an interview.
He said the Water Works Department will have to address the issue on an urgent basis, pending completion of a water supply project in Selangor in 1999 which will alleviate the problem.
The water supply for Selangor state and Kuala Lumpur currently totals 2.55 billion litres a day, the company said in its listing prospectus.
He said Selangor will have to import water from neighbouring Malaysian states by 2015 as its water resources would be fully utilised by then.

Puncak Niaga has a concession to operate, maintain, manage and refurbish existing water treatment plants in Selangor state in the the federal territory of Kuala Lumpur which encompasses the capital city. The 26-year concession will end on December 31, 2020.
Selangor state, which surrounds Kuala Lumpur, is one of Malaysia's fastest-growing states, with an annual average population growth of 3.8 percent between 1991 and 1995.
The state's population in 1995 stood at 2.8 million people with another 1.3 million people living in Kuala Lumpur.
Rozali said Puncak Niaga expects to be listed on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange by mid-July, the first water concession holder to be listed in Malaysia.
The company is offering 67 million new and existing shares to the public, with the retail tranche offered at 3.80 ringgit each and the institutional tranche at 4.50 ringgit.
